Definition: from G3708; something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural):--sight, vision.
BiblicalUsage: hórama is the word for sight, vision. I meet it 12 times across the Bible, and Matthew is a good place to see it plainly. It says what it says, and I take it at face value.
TheologicalSignificance: What hórama tells me is that God speaks in visions, and His visions always come true. What I take from it is this — the plain sense is the safe sense.
RelatedEvents: The Burning Bush; The Conversion of Paul
